clue.text: A Spanish port's unknown language

parts.note: Malaga is a port on Spain's southern coast; with the possessive it gives MALAGA'S
Y is one of the algebraic letters standing for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A question about what tongue the people of a Spanish harbour town speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish port suggests Spanish or Catalan, but its name is simply the start of the island tongue of Madagascar.
explanation.definitionFit: Malagasy is the Austronesian tongue spoken in Madagascar.

clue.text: Periodical defending the Italian graduate holding the post

indicators.note: defending means the magazine surrounds the next pieces, guarding them

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical
il is Italian for the
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A magazine sticks up for an Italian graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: A mailbag holds letters, which the British call the post.

clue.text: Remains of tea, say, brewed in bars

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters sit inside the bars

parts.note: levers are bars, as with crowbars

indicators.note: brewed means the letters are stewed into a new order

parts.note: the letter T is said like the word tea

explanation.surface: The dregs of a pot of tea brewed in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea, say' is the letter T by sound; 'brewed' scrambles it with 'of', and 'in' places the result inside the bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftovers are what remains uneaten after a meal.

clue.text: Undergo change as a reward

indicators.note: change means the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being transformed as a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Guerdon is an old literary word for a recompense.

clue.text: Greater London borough supporting society ball

indicators.note: in a down answer supporting means placed underneath, so the district comes below

parts.note: Pinner is a suburb of north-west London, in the borough of Harrow

explanation.surface: A London borough backs a society dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance, but it is a cricket ball that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a spinner is a delivery bowled with spin.

clue.text: He wrote directions about a card-game

indicators.note: about means the compass letters are placed around the game's name

parts.note: S and E are compass points, south and east
crib is short for cribbage, a card game scored on a pegboard

explanation.surface: Someone wrote out the rules for a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a copyist, a person whose job was writing documents by hand.

clue.text: He has loads to do in Everest trip

indicators.note: in means the word do goes inside the rearranged letters
trip suggests a stumble, so the letters of the mountain fall out of order

explanation.surface: A mountaineer has plenty to do on an Everest expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He has loads' sounds like a busy person but is a docker; 'trip' scrambles the mountain and 'in' plants 'do' in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships at a dock.

clue.text: Particular relation

definitions.meaning: a particular is a detail or point

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a point or detail, and reference or regard to something.

clue.text: The old country way is to have tea outside

indicators.note: outside means the tea goes around the road

parts.note: bohea is a kind of black China tea
M1 is the motorway from London north, written MI

explanation.surface: A traditional rural custom of drinking tea outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old country' suggests a homeland; it is Bohemia, a historic kingdom now in Czechia.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia was a former kingdom of central Europe.

clue.text: In following Roman Law, one bishop the French found obdurate

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
lex is the Latin word for law
I is the Roman numeral for one
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone sticking to Roman law and a French bishop proved unbending.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate and inflexible are synonyms for stubbornly unyielding.

clue.text: Some returning to hospital in central London

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some patients going back to a hospital in the middle of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks OHOS out of 'to hospital' and 'returning' reads it backwards. Soho is a district of the West End.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of the West End, in the heart of the capital.

clue.text: American woman spotlit as being wide-hipped

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman
caught in a light beam, i.e. in the beam

explanation.surface: A woman from the States standing under a spotlight is described as having large hips.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad in the beam is an idiom, from a ship's width, for having wide hips.

clue.text: Man returns without list, one gathers

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the turned name wraps the next piece
returns means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, short for Reginald
to list is to lean, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A man comes back with no list, as one who collects things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense outside; 'returns' turns the man's name before it wraps the list.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner collects leftover grain from a harvested field, or gathers facts.

clue.text: The sort of insurance women tend to be put off

indicators.note: put off means the letters are disturbed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Women tend to be discouraged from a type of life cover.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment policy is a type of life cover paying out on a set date.

clue.text: Base lodging for a robber

parts.note: the foot of something is its base
pad is slang for one's lodging or flat

explanation.surface: A base used as lodgings by a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpad was a highwayman on foot, a street thief of old.

clue.text: Abstract, see? Quite so

parts.note: a precis is an abstract or summary
Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop, hence a see

explanation.surface: A summary? Exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Precisely is used as an agreeing response meaning exactly.

clue.text: Engineer catching a fish in a small waterfall

indicators.note: catching means the engineer's letters hold the next pieces inside

parts.note: CE stands for Civil Engineer
the scad is a fish, the horse mackerel

explanation.surface: An engineer lands a fish at a little falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a small steep fall of water, often one of a series.

clue.text: Ways gunners built up a weapon store

indicators.note: built up in a down answer means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: lanes are ways, narrow roads
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: Ways for gunners to build up an armoury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gunners' also suggests the football club nicknamed the Gunners, which is the answer's other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a place where arms and ammunition are kept.

clue.text: Concern about container for a rifle

indicators.note: about means the concern goes around the container

parts.note: care is concern
a bin is a container

explanation.surface: Worry over the case for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbine is a short light rifle.

clue.text: Girl taking an age to find a tile

parts.note: Tess is a girl's name
an era is an age

explanation.surface: A girl takes ages hunting for a tile.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is a small block of stone or glass used in mosaics.

clue.text: Josip Broz's detailed standard to measure concentration

indicators.note: detailed means having lost its tail, the last letter

parts.note: Josip Broz was the Yugoslav leader known as Tito
a rate is a standard, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Tito's precise norm for gauging strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' seems to mean thorough, but it cuts the tail off TITO.
explanation.definitionFit: To titrate is to find the strength of a solution by adding a reagent.

clue.text: One of those imperfect witches in Macbeth?

definitions.text: One of those imperfect witches in Macbeth?

parts.words: One of those imperfect witches in Macbeth?
parts.note: Macbeth addresses the three witches as 'you imperfect' talkers, wanting them to say more

explanation.surface: A quiz question about the weird sisters in Shakespeare's Scottish play.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth tells the witches 'Stay, you imperfect speakers, tell me more', so each is one of those.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth calls the witches 'imperfect' talkers for their half-told prophecy, so each is one such talker.

clue.text: Accountant said on the Continent to be surrounded by gold

indicators.note: to be surrounded by means the French word sits between the golds

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
or is gold in heraldry, and the French word for it
dit is French for said

explanation.surface: An accountant, as they say in Europe, is ringed with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: One word 'gold' supplies two pieces, the chemical symbol and the heraldic or French word, which flank the French for said.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor checks the financial books of a company, as a kind of bookkeeper.

clue.text: Hint of recurring skin trouble among orchestral musicians

indicators.note: recurring read as running back, so the skin complaint is turned round

parts.note: warts are growths on the skin
the wind are the woodwind and brass players of an orchestra, so among them is in the wind

explanation.surface: A sign of a skin complaint that keeps coming back among the orchestra's players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recurring' suggests an illness coming back, but it turns the skin trouble round.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw in the wind is a small sign of what is coming, an indication.

clue.text: One opposed to high jinks the Civil Service suppressed

indicators.note: suppressed means those letters are removed

parts.note: antics are high jinks, playful pranks
CS is the abbreviation for Civil Service

explanation.surface: Someone who disapproved of horseplay that the Civil Service hushed up.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is a person who is against something, an opponent.

clue.text: Financiers possibly met about the Thames-side carriage-way

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the financiers
possibly suggests the word met may be arranged another way

parts.note: bankmen are people in banking, financiers

explanation.surface: Some financiers met to talk about the road along the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges 'met' and 'about' wraps it round the financiers. The Embankment is a road on the Thames bank in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Embankment is a road running beside the river in central London.

clue.text: Customer's legal right observed in Connecticut

indicators.note: observed in means the legal right is seen inside the state's letters

parts.note: CT is the postal abbreviation for Connecticut
a lien is a right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A customer's legal rights are honoured in Connecticut.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Customer's' stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is a person buying a service, a patron.

clue.text: He gives away a beret extremely reluctantly, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says these letters could be arranged otherwise
extremely picks the first and last letters of reluctantly

explanation.surface: Someone who hands over a beret with great unwillingness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives RY, the first and last letters of 'reluctantly', which join A and BERET; 'perhaps' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor gives away secrets or friends to an enemy.
